PRESS RELEASE — October 15, 2024

Veridian Mobility Reports Third Quarter Results; Raw Material Headwinds Persist

LONDON — Veridian Mobility PLC today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2024. Revenue came in at £1.42 billion, down 4.3% year-over-year, as surging raw material costs and weakening demand in the European commercial vehicle market weighed on performance.

Chief Executive Officer Armand Leroy attributed the decline primarily to unprecedented increases in natural rubber and carbon black prices, which began accelerating in the second quarter of 2024 and have continued to intensify. "The raw material cost spike that started in Q2 2024 is now flowing fully through our cost of goods," said Leroy. "We expect this to compress our gross margins by approximately 150 basis points over the next two quarters until we can renegotiate our long-term supply contracts."

Despite the near-term headwinds, management pointed to a record order backlog of £3.1 billion in connected fleet services as a leading indicator of future recurring revenue growth. Fleet telematics subscriptions grew 22% year-over-year, driven by regulatory tailwinds in the EU requiring real-time emissions monitoring from January 2025. "Our subscription pipeline gives us confidence in earnings recovery through 2025," Leroy added.

The company also noted that the October 2024 closure of its Clermont-Ferrand legacy facility will generate annual fixed-cost savings of approximately £45 million beginning in fiscal year 2025, partially offsetting the raw material pressure.

Shares of Veridian Mobility fell 3.2% in early London trading following the release.
